name: North Carolina
tagline: From the Smokies to the Outer Banks, by way of mill towns, pottery kilns and tobacco country.
intro: North Carolina's byways climb the Blue Ridge and the Great Smokies, wind through Piedmont farm country and pottery towns, and run out along the sounds to the Outer Banks. This chapter follows the North Carolina Byways Program, run by the North Carolina Department of Transportation, whose guidebook describes every route; the national forest byway in the Nantahala is listed separately because it comes from a different program.

members.name: Airlie Road
members.blurb: A mile and a half under moss-hung oaks past Airlie Gardens, where the gatekeeper Minnie Evans painted, opening at the end onto marsh grass and boat docks at the Wrightsville drawbridge.
members.note: Route line from NCDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Alligator River Route
members.blurb: NC 94 crosses Lake Mattamuskeet on a six-mile causeway among migrating waterfowl, then runs north through swamp and reclaimed farmland to Columbia and east along the Alligator River refuge.

members.name: Appalachian Medley
members.blurb: NC 209 winds north from Lake Junaluska through the hamlets of Luck and Trust, where a general store keeps the crossroads, then down Spring Creek to Hot Springs and the Appalachian Trail.

members.name: Averasboro Battlefield Byway
members.blurb: Five miles of NC 82 across farmland that was woods when Sherman's army fought here near the end of the Civil War, past re-created trench lines and a plantation house that served as a Confederate hospital.

members.name: Big Horse Creek Byway
members.blurb: From Lansing, an old Creeper railroad town, the road follows Big Horse Creek north, crossing it again and again past barns and country churches, and turns to gravel before the Virginia line.
members.note: Route line from NCDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Birkhead Wilderness Route
members.blurb: Randolph County roads along the edge of the Birkhead Mountain Wilderness, where pioneer chimneys stand in the woods, with a side road to the Pisgah Covered Bridge, built in 1911 for forty dollars.

members.name: Black Mountain Rag
members.blurb: Named for an old fiddle tune, NC 9 twists south from Black Mountain to the hamlet of Bat Cave, then runs under the granite knob of Chimney Rock to the still water of Lake Lure.

members.name: Blue Ridge Parkway
members.blurb: Two hundred fifty-two miles of New Deal parkway along the crest from the Virginia line to Cherokee, through 26 tunnels and up past 6,000 feet at Richland Balsam.

members.name: Blue-Gray Byway
members.blurb: Out of Four Oaks on Devils Racetrack Road to the Bentonville battlefield of March 1865, then across the Neuse farmlands to the old spring resort at Seven Springs and on to Trenton.

members.name: Brunswick Town Road
members.blurb: A short road south of Wilmington past Orton Plantation, where alligators sometimes sun beside the pavement, ending at the roofless ruins of St. Philip's church among the Civil War bunkers of Fort Anderson.

members.name: Cape Fear Historic Byway
members.blurb: A slow loop through Wilmington's 1743 street grid, down the Riverwalk with the battleship North Carolina moored across the water, then out around the lake in Greenfield Park.

members.name: Carolina Bay Lakes Byway
members.blurb: NC 242 runs south from Spiveys Corner, home of a hollerin' contest, through farm country to Elizabethtown, near oval lakes long blamed on meteors and now thought to be the work of wind and water.
members.note: Listed as Meteor Lakes Byway in the 2022 national dataset.

members.name: Cherohala Skyway
members.blurb: NC 143 climbs from Santeetlah Gap to the Tennessee line past grassy balds, among them Hooper's Bald at 5,429 feet, where wild boar loosed for an old hunting preserve still root in the woods.

members.name: Clayton Bypass Scenic Byway
members.blurb: One of two freeways in the state with scenic byway status, nine miles of US 70 around Clayton with long straightaways over pasture and woodlots in Johnston County farm country.
members.note: Route line from NCDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Colonial Heritage Byway
members.blurb: A long ramble through Piedmont dairy country along the routes Greene and Cornwallis took in 1781, past brick general stores of the 1800s and the river town of Milton to colonial Hillsborough.

members.name: Crowders Mountain Drive
members.blurb: Eight miles of back road around the foot of Crowders Mountain and the Pinnacle, worn-down knobs of the old Appalachians standing above the countryside near Kings Mountain.

members.name: Devil's Tramping Ground Road
members.blurb: NC 902 leaves the Pittsboro courthouse for the lower Piedmont, crossing the Rocky River near Bear Creek, where a bare ring in the woods is said to be worn by the devil's pacing.
members.note: Listed as Devil's Stompin' Ground Road in the 2022 national dataset.

members.name: Drovers Road
members.blurb: US 74A drops from Fairview through Hickory Nut Gap, the pass where drovers once herded livestock to market, past Sherrill's old inn and the hamlet of Gerton, once called Pump, to Bat Cave.

members.name: East Connecticut Avenue
members.blurb: A short, curving avenue out of Southern Pines through longleaf pine and horse farms, past the Weymouth Woods preserve, where one pine dates to 1548, ending at the Fort Bragg gate.
members.note: Route line from NCDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Edenton-Windsor Loop
members.blurb: A figure-eight out of Edenton, the old tea-party town, across the two-mile-wide Chowan and over the Cashie on the two-car Sans Souci cable ferry to Windsor and back around the Albemarle.

members.name: Flint Hill Ramble
members.blurb: Four miles of winding forest road through old gold country near Ophir, past the north end of the Uwharrie Trail and a rocky bluff the locals call Jumping Off Rock.

members.name: Fontana Byway
members.blurb: NC 28 leaves Deals Gap for the shore of Cheoah Lake and the TVA's Fontana Dam, finished in 1945, then passes surge pipes running straight up the slopes near Stecoah on the way to Franklin.
members.note: Listed as Indian Lakes Scenic Byway in the 2022 national dataset.

members.name: Football Road
members.blurb: The back way Greensboro fans once drove to games in Chapel Hill, past small dairy farms and ponds and through Snow Camp, a Quaker settlement since 1749.

members.name: Forest Heritage Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 276 climbs out of Brevard into Pisgah National Forest, past Looking Glass Falls, sixty feet high beside the road, and the Cradle of Forestry, where America's first forestry school began in 1898.

members.name: French Broad Overview
members.blurb: NC 251 follows the French Broad down from Weaverville on an old trading path, under sheer rock palisades, to Marshall, a river town of 1852 with a single bridge across the water.

members.name: Grassy Island Crossing
members.blurb: Country roads on both sides of the Pee Dee, named for Grassy Island, a cluster of earthen islets in the river, through pine woods and swamp near the inland wildlife refuge at Ansonville.

members.name: Green Swamp Byway
members.blurb: NC 211 runs north from Supply through the Green Swamp, in and out of shrub bogs and open longleaf savanna where Venus flytraps and pitcher plants grow wild.

members.name: Highlands of the Roan Byway
members.blurb: Past Christmas tree farms and the Toe River, NC 261 climbs out of Bakersville to Carvers Gap, where the Roan's wild Catawba rhododendrons turn the slopes magenta in late June.
members.note: Route line from NCDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Historic Flat Rock Byway
members.blurb: Back roads through the village Charleston families called the Little Charleston of the mountains, past the 1836 church of St. John in the Wilderness and Connemara, Carl Sandburg's home and goat barn.

members.name: Indian Heritage Trail
members.blurb: From the old spa town of Ellerbe through peach orchards and roadside fruit stands to Town Creek, where the Pee Dee people's ceremonial mound and temples stand rebuilt near Mount Gilead.

members.name: Interstate 26 Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Nine miles of interstate from Mars Hill to Sams Gap, climbing to nearly 5,000 feet at Buckner Gap and crossing the Laurel River on the state's tallest bridge, which de-ices itself.

members.name: Lafayette's Tour
members.blurb: A long eastward run through the river towns Lafayette visited in 1825, from the antebellum houses of Warrenton to colonial Halifax, crossing the Meherrin on a two-car cable ferry.

members.name: Little Parkway
members.blurb: US 221 follows the Yonahlossee Trail, an 1889 toll road cut by men and mules, around the flank of Grandfather Mountain from Linville to Blowing Rock, with the Linn Cove Viaduct in view.

members.name: McAuley Road Scenic Byway
members.blurb: A mile and a half of dirt road in fast-growing Mecklenburg County, crossing Ramah Creek on a one-lane wooden bridge between pastures and woods that look much as the county did a century ago.
members.note: Route line from NCDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Mill Bridge Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Rowan County farm roads west of Salisbury, past Kerr's grist mill of 1823 and the old Thyatira Presbyterian church, with quilt blocks painted on the barns around Mount Ulla.

members.name: Mission Crossing
members.blurb: NC 194 runs through ski country by way of an old toll turnpike and Banner Elk, then drops into the Watauga valley at Valle Crucis, with its Episcopal mission and the Mast General Store of 1882.

members.name: Mt. Mitchell Scenic Drive
members.blurb: From the 6,684-foot summit of Mount Mitchell the drive descends by NC 80 into the South Toe valley and on to Burnsville, where quilt squares hang on barns and Otway Burns stands in the square.
members.note: Route line from NCDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Nantahala Byway
members.blurb: From the quarry town of Marble, US 74 follows the Nantahala River into the gorge the Cherokee called the Land of the Midday Sun, with rafts on the water and an excursion train beside the road.

members.name: New River Valley Byway
members.blurb: NC 194 leaves Boone on the old Buffalo Trail, past Christmas tree farms and the logging village of Todd, along a north-flowing river believed to be the oldest in North America.

members.name: Newfound Gap Road Scenic Byway
members.blurb: US 441 climbs out of Cherokee along the Oconaluftee River, past the 1886 Mingus Mill, to the spruce and fir at Newfound Gap, where Roosevelt dedicated the Smokies park in 1940.
members.note: Route line from NCDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: North Durham Country Byway
members.blurb: North of Durham the road passes the Stagville plantation lands to the crossroads of Bahama, named from three family names, and runs along Bahama Road beside Lake Michie.

members.name: Outer Banks National Scenic Byway
members.blurb: NC 12 runs south from Whalebone Junction down the barrier islands past the striped Hatteras light, then takes two ferries across Pamlico Sound to the workboat harbors of Atlantic and on to Beaufort.

members.name: Pacolet River Byway
members.blurb: US 176 climbs from Tryon to Saluda through the frost-shy Thermal Belt, crossing the Pacolet River again and again beside the Saluda Grade, the steepest standard-gauge mainline railroad grade in the country.

members.name: Pamlico Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From the Pamlico River at Washington to Bath, the state's oldest town, then out US 264 through drained farmland and three wildlife refuges, forty miles without a gas station past Engelhard.

members.name: Pee Dee Valley Drive
members.blurb: From Badin, an aluminum company town of French-style townhouses, the drive follows the Pee Dee south past Morrow Mountain to Norwood on the shore of Lake Tillery.

members.name: Perquimans Crossing
members.blurb: Two miles of old US 17 into Hertford over the Perquimans River on an S-shaped swing bridge, believed to be the last of its kind still working, with a house of about 1730 a short way beyond.

members.name: Pisgah Loop Byway
members.blurb: A Burke County loop that climbs from Morganton into Pisgah National Forest and runs fifteen unpaved miles along Linville Gorge, under Table Rock and Hawksbill, before settling at Lake James.

members.name: Pottery Road
members.blurb: NC 705 runs north under the old cedars at Eagle Springs to Seagrove, through Whynot and Jugtown, where descendants of 18th-century Staffordshire potters still turn pots.

members.name: Roanoke Voyages Corridor
members.blurb: Seven miles across Roanoke Island, where the Lost Colony vanished, past the Waterside Theater and into Manteo, with the Elizabeth II tied up across the harbor.

members.name: Rolling Kansas Byway
members.blurb: Nine miles of Stanly County back road out of Richfield, over hills nicknamed Rolling Kansas for their old farms and windmills, to the Bethel Bear Creek church and its graves from the 1820s.

members.name: Sandhills Scenic Drive
members.blurb: NC 24/27 runs west from the old Scots town of Carthage over sandy ridges and farmland to Troy, then crosses the Pee Dee by Lake Tillery between two worn Uwharrie peaks.

members.name: Sauratown Mountains Scenic Byway
members.blurb: From Mount Airy, the model for Mayberry, the road wanders the old Sauratown range past Hanging Rock and the granite Moratock furnace at Danbury, then circles the foot of Pilot Mountain's quartzite pinnacle.
members.note: Listed as Hanging Rock Scenic Byway in the 2022 national dataset.

members.name: Scots-Welsh Heritage Byway
members.blurb: Orange County farm roads that follow a colonial highway and an old trading path, partly on gravel past log cabins, to a crossroads store known for its homemade ice cream.

members.name: South Mountain Scenery
members.blurb: NC 226 runs from the farms north of Shelby toward Marion, through corn fields and apple orchards, with the South Mountains rising ahead and Cherry Mountain, named for an old cherry liquor, off to the southwest.

members.name: Tar Heel Trace
members.blurb: Coastal Plain roads from Wilson through old pine-tar country, past Conetoe, said Cuh-knee-ta, among soybean and peanut fields, with peanut sheds and silos thickening toward Williamston.

members.name: The College Town Ride
members.blurb: Down Davidson's Main Street past the 1837 college and the old Helper Hotel, then out among Piedmont barns and pastures to Fisher Farm Park, a short ride well known to weekend cyclists.
members.note: Route line from NCDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Turkey Creek Byway
members.blurb: Eleven miles of US 264 through pine and hardwood, where highway builders in the early 1970s left a wide median so Turkey Creek could keep its own course between the lanes.
members.note: Route line from NCDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: U.S. 421 Scenic Highway
members.blurb: Eight miles of US 421 from Deep Gap, home of Doc Watson, toward Boone, beginning under a stone-faced Parkway bridge and climbing past rows of Fraser fir grown for Christmas.

members.name: Upper Yadkin Way
members.blurb: NC 268 follows the young Yadkin through the farms of Happy Valley, past Fort Defiance, William Lenoir's house of 1790, and the 1962 reservoir at Goshen to Wilkesboro.

members.name: Uwharrie Scenic Road
members.blurb: NC 49 crosses the Carolina Slate Belt and the worn volcanic hills of the Uwharries between Asheboro and Concord, through corn and winter wheat, where slate once went into buildings and fences.

members.name: Waterfall Byway
members.blurb: US 64 runs west from Rosman through Cashiers and Highlands, then down the Cullasaja Gorge, where Bridal Veil Falls drops 45 feet within a few yards of the pavement, and on to Murphy's marble courthouse.

members.name: Whitewater Way
members.blurb: Eight miles of NC 281 drop south from Sapphire through hemlock and spruce toward the South Carolina line, with a short walk to Whitewater Falls, a fall of 411 feet.

members.name: Yadkin Valley Scenic Byway
members.blurb: Old tobacco country along the Yadkin, now planted in vineyards, with the knob of Pilot Mountain in view for much of the drive and old country stores on the back roads to Elkin.
members.note: Route line from NCDOT (not in the 2022 national dataset).

members.name: Forest Heritage National Scenic Byway
members.note: The nationally designated section of the Forest Heritage Scenic Byway, which the 2022 national dataset lists as a separate road.

sources.label: NCDOT, North Carolina Scenic Byways guidebook (5th edition)
